newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum premiums feel a summer softness.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum premiums feel a summer softness.

text.p: Aluminum premiums in the United States remain a touch soft with further weakening on the back of a seasonal lull expected by some dealers.
"The bloom is off the rose," a Midwest aluminum merchant said.
The sale of spot metal by the U.S. Stockpile has not helped sentiment, the merchant added.
Dealers said spot aluminum premiums were 4.25 to 5.00 cents a lb over LME cash - a wider spread than in recent weeks, though most of the business appeared to be in a narrower 4.50 to 5.00 cent range.
"Business is still good and we have been able to get 5.00 cents," a New York aluminum broker said.

Jim Southwood of Commodity Metal Management said despite a recent slight recovery in canstock, overall U.S. aluminum order rates have been declining since the end of March because the growth rate was unsustainable and because of seasonal factors.
"Premiums are weaker and getting weaker," Southwood said.
The weakened contango on LME made it difficult to finance metal, thereby prompting some dealers to offload metal onto the market.
The contango was still too weak to finance metal in the medium to long term, therefore premiums, and in turn LME prices, will continue to come under pressure, Southwood said.

The 200,000 tonne drop in LME aluminum stocks since the start of the year has not been consumed, Southwood said. Some 100,000 tonnes went to Hungary to beat a duty change at the end of June, with the balance exported to the U.S., consumed or moved off exchange for storage.
Zinc premiums remain stable at 4.50 to 4.75 cents a lb over LME cash after their recent post-Mint tender decline.
"Business is good and supply remains tight," a broker said.
Premiums in nickel and tin also remained largely unchanged from last week's levels.
